author: Brianna Kelly
title: Work begins soon to transform St. Louis Park restaurant into Chi-Chi's - NewsBreak
text: At the end of August, Rojo Mexican Grill will shutter in St. Louis Park ’s West End, and work will get underway on Chi-Chi's first restaurant in over 20 years. Rojo owner Michael McDermott secured the rights to reopen Chi-Chi's restaurants in late 2024. He's the son of Chi-Chi's co-founder Marno McDermott, who launched the brand in 1975 alongside former Green Bay Packers player Max McGee and helped it go public in 1979. Chi-Chi's started in Minnesota and eventually expanded to more than 200 locations nationwide. However, it declared bankruptcy following a hepatitis A outbreak traced to green onions at a Pennsylvania location. All of its restaurants were closed by 2004. Now, Chi-Chi's is poised to make its comeback before the end of 2025, with construction on Rojo's space slated to start at the beginning of September. "Chi-Chi's is coming back stronger than ever," Michael McDermott said in a statement on Tuesday. "We’re bringing back the food, the energy, and the fun that made Chi-Chi's a household name and giving it a fresh twist for a whole new generation." McDermott previously told Bring Me The News that his Chi-Chi's revival will serve most, if not all of the dishes that diners remember, including his personal favorite, the Deep-Fried Red Chili Burro served enchilada-style. The menu also features some of Rojo's signature dishes, plus birria tacos and other new items. McDermott created Rojo as an elevated version of Chi-Chi's in 2010. He also founded Kona Grill, an Arizona-based chain with a location in Eden Prairie , and Tavern23 in Edina . Rojo's other location in Maple Grove is slated for conversion into Chi-Chi's as well. After that, franchisees could open other Chi-Chi's restaurants across the U.S., including former franchisees who are eager to take part in the comeback. McDermott said he wants to focus on the Midwest and East Coast to start. A crowdfunding campaign on StartEngine has raised more than $2 million for the Chi-Chi's relaunch. McDermott initially hoped to collect $3.5 million and offer equity to investors who contribute at least $250. Hormel Foods plans to continue making and selling its Chi-Chi's brand salsas, tortillas, and seasonings in grocery stores.
